JavaScript

Interactive components use plain data attributes and a runtime of under 400 lines with no dependencies. It works on any HTML: server-rendered pages, htmx swaps, or markup rendered by a client framework.

Loading

Every behavior is an ES module that imports ./velle.js and starts working as soon as it loads. The CLI imports the behaviors you install in main.js, so one <script type="module" src="/assets/js/velle/main.js"> is enough. To include them yourself:

<script type="module" src="/assets/js/velle/dialog.js"></script>
<script type="module" src="/assets/js/velle/tabs.js"></script>

Or load the bundle, which contains the runtime and every behavior:

<script type="module" src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/codedbyshoe/velle-css@v{{.Site.Version}}/dist/velle.js"></script>

The bundle leaves out the adapters. To use one with the bundle, load it from dist/adapters/, next to dist/velle.js; those copies import ../velle.js and share its runtime.

Elements are set up when the page loads and whenever matching markup is added later. A MutationObserver watches the document, so nothing needs to be re-initialized after content changes.

Using the JavaScript without the CSS

The behaviors work on any markup and don't need velle's stylesheets. To keep styles out of a project entirely:

velle init --js           # writes velle.json and main.js, and no styles
velle add tabs menu       # copies only their JavaScript
velle new controller cart # or start from the bare runtime

Without the CLI, dist/js/velle.js is the runtime alone and dist/velle.js is the runtime with every behavior. Neither loads any CSS.

Styling is then yours. Behaviors expose their state through ARIA and standard attributes such as aria-selected, hidden and open. A few also use class names or need a particular layout: each of those component pages says what it expects under Notes, and velle add prints the same note. Treat the data attributes on each component page as the behavior's public API.

Attributes

Each behavior has a name, such as tabs or check-all, and reads these attributes:

AttributePurposeExample
data-NAMEMarks the root element. Each root gets its own controller instance.<div data-tabs>
data-NAME-targetNames an element inside the root that the behavior uses. Several names can be separated by spaces.data-tabs-target="button"
data-NAME-actionConnects events to the behavior's actions. Can sit on the root or anything inside it.data-tabs-action="select"
data-NAME-OPTIONAn option read from the root.data-tabs-index="2"
data-NAME-PARAM-paramA value passed to an action as event.params.PARAM.data-form-submitter-param="save"

Roots can be nested. A target or action always belongs to the closest root with the same name.

Action syntax

[event[.keyfilter][@document|@window]->]action[:prevent][:stop][:self]
PartMeaning
eventAny DOM event name, including custom events. When omitted, the element's default event is used: click for buttons and links, input for inputs and textareas (click for submit inputs), change for selects, submit for forms and toggle for <details>.
.keyfilterFor keydown, keyup and keypress: only run for this key. Keys: any single character, such as k or 7, or enter, tab, esc, space, up, down, left, right, home, end, page_up, page_down. Prefix with ctrl+, meta+, alt+ or shift+; modifiers must match exactly.
@document, @windowListen on the document or window instead of the element, e.g. for keyboard shortcuts and outside clicks.
:preventCalls event.preventDefault() before the action.
:stopCalls event.stopPropagation() before the action.
:selfOnly runs when the event's target is the element itself, not a descendant.

Separate several actions with spaces:

<textarea data-form-action="keydown.ctrl+enter->submit keydown.meta+enter->submit"></textarea>

Events

Behaviors announce changes with bubbling CustomEvents named velle:NAME:EVENT, dispatched from the root element. Each component page lists its events.

document.addEventListener("velle:tabs:change", event => {
  console.log("Selected tab", event.detail.index)
})

Writing your own controllers

Use controller({ targets, values }) as the base class for behavior specific to your app. velle new controller cart creates a file to start from and imports it in main.js.

This example has a counter and a cart badge that follows it:

<div data-counter>
  <output data-counter-target="output"></output>
  <button data-counter-action="increment">Add to cart</button>
</div>

<nav data-cart data-cart-count="0" data-cart-action="velle:counter:change@window->refresh">
  <span class="badge" data-cart-target="badge"></span>
  <span data-cart-target="total"></span>
</nav>
// @ts-check
import { define, controller } from "./velle.js"

define("counter", class extends controller({
  targets: { output: HTMLElement },
  values: { count: 0 },
}) {
  connect() {
    this.countChanged()
  }

  increment() {
    this.count++
  }

  countChanged() {
    const { output } = this.$
    if (output) output.textContent = String(this.count)
    this.dispatch("change", { count: this.count })
  }
})

define("cart", class extends controller({
  targets: { badge: HTMLElement, total: HTMLElement },
  values: { count: 0, url: "/cart/total" },
}) {
  connect() {
    this.on(document, "visibilitychange", () => this.#loadTotal())
    this.countChanged()
  }

  /** @param {CustomEvent<{ count: number }>} event */
  refresh(event) {
    this.count = event.detail.count
  }

  countChanged() {
    const { badge } = this.$
    if (badge) badge.textContent = String(this.count)
    this.#loadTotal()
  }

  async #loadTotal() {
    try {
      const response = await fetch(this.url, { signal: this.signal })
      const { total } = this.$
      if (total) total.textContent = await response.text()
    } catch (error) {
      if (!this.signal.aborted) throw error
    }
  }
})

Targets. targets maps each name to the element class you expect. this.$.total is the first match or null, this.$$.total is an array, and an undeclared name is a type error.

Values. values maps each name to its default, and the default's type decides how the attribute is parsed: numbers, strings, booleans (present means true, "false" means false), or JSON for arrays and objects. this.count reads data-cart-count and assigning to it writes the attribute; showMonths maps to data-NAME-show-months. Names the controller already uses, such as data, element, target and action, throw an error.

Callbacks. countChanged(value, oldValue) runs after the attribute changes, whoever changed it. It runs asynchronously and never during connect(), so call it from connect() to render the initial state.

Styling. State lives in attributes, so CSS can read it directly:

[data-cart-count="0"] .badge { display: none }

Cleanup. this.on(target, type, listener, options) adds a listener that is removed when the controller disconnects. this.signal aborts at the same moment; pass it to fetch(url, { signal: this.signal }) or anything else that accepts one.

Talking to other controllers. Actions accept any event name, so one controller can listen for another's dispatch() with data-cart-action="velle:counter:change@window->refresh".

Reaching a controller from outside. controllerFor(element, name) returns the connected instance or null, for htmx hooks and inline scripts. Its result is a plain Controller to the type checker, so annotate it to use your own properties:

import { controllerFor } from "./velle.js"

/** @type {any} */
const cart = controllerFor(document.querySelector("[data-cart]"), "cart")
if (cart) cart.count = 0

Saved copies of the page. Libraries that keep a copy of the page, such as htmx for its history, save whatever your controllers have added to it. If connect() builds markup that it would build again on the restored copy, define beforeSnapshot() to remove it and return a function that puts it back:

beforeSnapshot() {
  const widget = this.$.widget
  widget?.remove()
  return () => { if (widget) this.element.append(widget) }
}

Several controllers on one element. Each name gets its own instance, and an action goes to the controller its attribute names:

<form data-form data-autosave data-form-action="keydown.ctrl+enter->submit">

Editor setup. velle.d.ts sits next to velle.js, and velle new controller writes this jsconfig.json at the project root unless you already have one. Start a file with // @ts-check to see errors for that file in any editor that uses TypeScript.

{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "checkJs": true,
    "strict": true,
    "module": "esnext",
    "target": "es2022",
    "moduleResolution": "bundler"
  }
}

Extensions

Extensions connect the runtime to other tools. They are optional, are installed only by name, and stay out of the bundles.

velle add htmx

Without the CLI, use the copy that matches your runtime so the page only ever loads one: dist/extensions/ with the dist/velle.js bundle, or dist/js/ next to dist/js/velle.js.

Each extension has a page under Extensions in the navigation.

Runtime API

The runtime exports what the built-in behaviors use, so your own code can follow the same conventions:

import { define, Controller } from "./velle.js"

// <div data-counter data-counter-start="5">
//   <output data-counter-target="count"></output>
//   <button data-counter-action="increment">+1</button>
// </div>
define("counter", class extends Controller {
  #count = 0

  connect() {
    this.#count = Number(this.data("start")) || 0
    this.#render()
  }

  increment() {
    this.#count++
    this.#render()
    this.dispatch("change", { count: this.#count })
  }

  #render() {
    this.target("count").textContent = this.#count
  }
})
ExportDescription
define(name, Class)Registers a controller class for data-NAME roots.
ControllerBase class. Provides this.element, connect(), disconnect(), target(name), targets(name), hasTarget(name), data(key), hasData(key), dispatch(type, detail), $, $$, on(target, type, listener, options) and signal. Define beforeSnapshot() to take part in prepareSnapshot(). Actions are called with the event and the element that declared the action.
controller({ targets, values })Builds a Controller subclass with typed targets and values stored in data attributes.
controllerFor(element, name)Returns the connected controller instance on an element, or null.
prepareSnapshot()Calls beforeSnapshot() on every connected controller and returns a function that undoes what they did. Call it just before saving a copy of the page.
observe(selector, { connect, disconnect })Runs callbacks when elements start or stop matching a selector. Use it for behaviors that need no root.
debounce(fn, wait)A trailing-edge debounce.

When you use the bundle, import from it instead: import { define, Controller } from "…/dist/velle.js".
